content.rationale: The decision is a page composition whose refs are code (media/webview.html, src/webview/main.ts), and the prerequisites it mounts are code artefacts too — the renderer (rtlotqvy), the search page module (uryrrttr), the interaction and keyboard state (noplrntp), the presentation (yruxqknp), the page interface (ympqvvwr), the graph model and order (qmsmvrnr), the detail-section behaviour (vqwoptmu, yrtrqutm, qwzwpxws, rmovtvkt), the toolbar action (mspmqvuk) and the page regions (zrqxuzzy) — so the code-to-code cell applies and the check is a runnable test. The composition test parses the real media/webview.html, adopts its body into jsdom, loads the source entry src/webview/main.ts into it and posts graphs across the page's message seam; it then drives the composed page as a user does: it reads the regions the page interface names, counts the node boxes and routed edges the renderer draws into the canvas layers, clicks a node and reads the detail region back, posts a warning and reads the banner, presses the toolbar's fit action and reads the viewport transform, presses `/` and reads a focused field, types a query and reads the match class on exactly the matching boxes, presses Enter and reads the newly selected box and its detail, presses Esc and reads the field, the marks and the selection gone, and posts a reload containing a node the query newly matches and reads the active query, the re-applied marks and the kept selection (including that only one search is attached). The detail test drives the same composed page for the detail panel it renders (vqwoptmu, yrtrqutm, qwzwpxws, rmovtvkt). The check names no composition function, field or event wiring the record does not fix: it finds the regions and the drawn identity through the page interface's exported selectors and attributes, the match emphasis through the search module's exported class, and the query field as the input the page puts over the canvas, so any page that mounts these modules and shows the committed behaviour passes. The refine adds two prerequisites whose content is words rather than an artefact — activating an id the panel lists selects the node it names and shows its detail as clicking its box does (kwxutvpw), and an id listed from an edge whose other end names no node document is listed but inert (rusopkql) — so those two edges sit in the natural-to-code (fidelity) cell, and the same runnable test carries them: the prose names observables, so fidelity can be applied by running the composed page instead of reading it, in both directions. The check reads every id a relationship section lists and activates it as a user does — a primary pointer pressed and released on the entry, then the compatibility click the browser adds and addresses to the element that captured the pointer if one holds it for that pointer and otherwise to the nearest common inclusive ancestor of the press and the release, and Enter and Space on the element around the entry that takes the keyboard focus — and requires the page to land on exactly the selection and the detail region a click on the node's own box gives, so the page enforces nothing less than the prose claims (kwxutvpw); and it requires an id whose edge names no node document to stay listed while the same pointer and key activation leave the selection and the detail region as they were, so the page adds nothing the prose does not allow and an inert entry never becomes a selection (rusopkql). Neither direction fixes a tag, a class, an attribute, a handler or a controller call: the id is found as the element that shows it inside the section its label names, the control as the element around it that takes the focus, and the observables read back are the page interface's own selection emphasis and the detail region the panel renders. The key press is applied the way a browser applies it, so the two inputs stay told apart: a native control the browser itself activates on a keypress — a button, a link with an href, a form button, a summary — is given the click the browser would fire, because jsdom runs none of that activation, while every other element is left to activate itself on the keydown, since for a span or a div that keyboard behaviour is the page's own obligation and a fallback click would hide a missing key handler. An entry that answered no key at all, or answered Enter and not Space, therefore fails the check even though the pointer gesture could carry it. The click a press and release ends in is addressed as a browser addresses it and not handed to the entry: jsdom runs no pointer capture, so the check keeps the browser's bookkeeping for it, and an entry the page can only reach by a click dispatched at it by hand — one sitting inside the element the page captures the pointer on, where a browser would address the click to the capturing element — is not activated by the check. The refine also retracts the composition's sentence that the entries add no appearance of their own, and adds eight prerequisites whose content is words over the mark the entries now carry: a listed id is presented as a visible link (mwwxxzyk), and that link takes the link colour role (tvoouwkn), the pointer cursor (rqrlnzny), the hover underline (qnmuwwvw) and the accent focus outline while it has the focus (vvzptxmz), while an entry whose id names no node document is drawn in the muted secondary role (mplxzxnm) and takes no pointer cursor, no hover underline and no focus outline (kpkstnps), and the markup and the stylesheet meet on one fixed vocabulary of two class names — detail__entry for the entry that names a node document and detail__entry--inert for the entry that names none, exactly one of the two on any listed entry and nothing beside it — the recorded pair is the whole vocabulary, so no third class, no further modifier on either name and no second entry name is on an entry (sqwusxql). Those eight edges are words over an artefact, so they sit in the natural-to-code (fidelity) cell and the same runnable test carries them: the composed page is run and the entries its panel renders are read back by the class each one carries, so the page enforces the mapping in both directions — every id a relationship section lists that names a node document carries detail__entry and every listed id that names none carries detail__entry--inert, with no listed entry left unclassified and none carrying both, and each entry's class list read whole rather than filtered down to the two recorded names: the element of the entry that shows the id carries its case's name alone, and no element of the entry spells a further name out of the two, so a third class or a further modifier added beside the case class is read as the extra name it is and the two recorded names are the whole of what an entry is marked with — and the declarations those classes select, the colour roles, the cursor, the hover rule, the focus outline and the muted role, are left to the check of the stylesheet that writes them, so this one neither restates them nor judges them. The check reads the two names from the record and not from the implementation, and names no element, selector or declaration: the class is read from the element that shows the id and the wrappers around it that show nothing else, so any page that marks its listed entries with the recorded vocabulary passes, whatever element of the entry carries it. The refine also adds two prerequisites whose content is words over the ref paths the Content section shows — a Content ref path is a control that opens that repo-relative file in the editor, activated by a pointer click or by Enter or Space while it has the focus (rptlovpt), and a ref-path entry carries detail__ref as its whole class, the one name the stylesheet's rules select (ppkkmxxu) — so those two edges sit in the natural-to-code (fidelity) cell, and the same two runnable tests carry them, because the composed page can be run rather than read and the prose names its observables: each direction is checked on the page the tests drive, and neither clause fixes a message name, a field name, a tag, a handler, a host-side resolution or failure rule, or a declaration. (a) The paths keep their place: the Content section still shows the content type and every path of a content.ref list in one monospaced block (qwzwpxws), and each of those paths is shown in that block as an entry of its own — the element that holds that path and nothing else, so the type and the list's other paths are not part of it — instead of as bare text in a block that holds them all, which both tests read off the composed page. (b) The entry's mark (ppkkmxxu): the class list of the element that shows the path is read whole and is detail__ref alone, and across the run of elements that hold that path no name is spelled out of it — no modifier on it and no second ref-path name — and neither of the two listed-entry names (detail__entry, detail__entry--inert) reaches a ref path, so the mark is that one name and nothing beside it; the mark is read from the element that shows the path, so any page that keeps the block and marks each path inside it passes, whatever element of the entry carries the name. (c) The activation and its request (rptlovpt): the entry is a control the keyboard can reach, and activating it posts, through the seam the page already declares, the page's request for that repo-relative path. The composition test drives the composed page the way a user does — the path activated by a pointer press and release, whose compatibility click is addressed where a browser addresses it, and, on the focused entry, by Enter and by Space — and reads the request off the page-to-host channel as one message that carries that path as a value of its own, naming neither the node nor the list's other path; where a native control is what the browser itself activates on a keypress it is given the click the browser would fire, and every other element is left to activate itself on the keydown, so an entry that answers no key, or Enter and not Space, fails the check although the pointer press and release could carry it. The activation is the ref path's own: the selection and the detail region the page shows stay as they were, because a path opens a file rather than selecting a node, and kwxutvpw's activation stays the listed ids'. How the host resolves and opens the path is the extension shell's own gate, and the declarations the detail__ref rules carry are the stylesheet's, so this one reads neither; the double-click on a node's box that opens its document (trxzsqpv) is left as it is and is not re-triggered by a ref path.
